findings: Alpha already scores lower-bound net expectancy, stressed-cost retention, return/drawdown efficiency, tail-risk economics, diversification, capacity utilization, parameter stability and bootstrap sign stability.

Turnover is transported as a finite non-negative scalar but has no horizon or notional normalization in CandidateEvidence or AdvancedAgentEvidence, so adding it directly to Alpha scoring would be scale-sensitive and economically ambiguous.
Capacity is represented only as capacity_utilization in [0,1]; the current contract does not bind participation rate, stressed market-impact bps, or a capacity-at-impact threshold.

The research adapter binds study/dataset/baseline hashes and derives normal/stressed expectancy from qualified fixed-holdout evidence, but turnover and capacity remain caller-supplied advanced evidence rather than derived from an auditable execution-economics model.
PR #2 remains open and collides with research_service.py; that shared path was not touched.
